title: Steps 3 to 7 QA
eyebrow: QA · #381 restructure steps 3 to 7, built as one feature · house-rules 2.74.0

short.lead: Restructure steps 3 to 7 (#381) are built on the branch AjsAgent/issue-281-fix as house-rules 2.74.0. Each step follows the grilling answers on the design page you approved. verify.py, the script that checks the hooks do what the docs say, passed all 966 checks. One thing matters before you install it: from 2.74.0, every tool is refused until the agent's name is set. So set the two cloud environment variables first (HOUSE_RULES_AGENT_NAME and HOUSE_RULES_OWNED_BRANCHES), using the steps in docs/cloud-session-setup.md.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what was built and how it was checked.
items: A settings script, scripts/settings.py, stores agent_name and extra_owned_prefixes. It reads environment variables first, then the file <config folder>/house-rules/settings.json, outside every repo.
Until both are set, every tool is refused except that script, and the refusal names the exact command. At session start the agent asks you, suggesting your GitHub login in lowercase plus "sAgent".
The credit lines ("Committed by <name>", "Opened by <name>"), the agent's branch prefix and the commit author now come from agent_name.

I tested it in a scratch home folder. "echo hi" was refused, the settings script saved both values, and then "echo hi" went through. With the two cloud environment variables set, the settings script's show command reports both values as coming from the environment.
Deleting a committed, unchanged file is allowed only on the agent's own branches, and refused elsewhere with the reason.
The automatic work-in-progress commits credit the agent name, with no Claude line.
An autosave snapshot branch is deleted once git shows that the helper agent's work on it has been merged.
The check that every tool needs the agent name set now refuses with a message, instead of doing nothing, on a machine without Python.
An issue whose text says "Part of #N" gets a reminder to link it as a sub-issue of #N on GitHub.
A second approval is refused while the previous approval's decisions-log entry was never written.
In a cloud session, a reply that links only a local page file is blocked: it must link the published claude.ai page.
An edit that replaces more than half of a file's lines needs your approval by name, like writing the whole file over.
A reply that skips a check because it is long, costs money, or needs an unreachable machine must ask you first.
A reply mentioning an unasked fix gets a note to make it an issue instead.
I ran both reply checks over 262 real replies from this session. The skip check wrongly fired once, so I narrowed it, and now it fires on none.
Helper agents run the parts of the code their change touched. They run them twice at the end of their work, and quote every RESULT and FAIL line in full.
A question only you can answer goes in the helper's report under the heading QUESTION FOR AJ, for me to ask you.
Autosave pushes each snapshot to a fresh branch without forcing it, and the cleanup deletes all of them.
Set the variables, then pass or fail QA
First, in each Claude account, add the two environment variables from docs/cloud-session-setup.md: HOUSE_RULES_AGENT_NAME=ajw2003sAgent and HOUSE_RULES_OWNED_BRANCHES=AjsAgent/,claude/.
After this ships, a new session should start without any refusal, and new commits should end with "Committed by ajw2003sAgent".

Not changed, on purpose: the GitHub label names such as "AjsAgent created this", because renaming them would strip them from every issue that already has them. The rules text still says "aj's agent" in places; that is prose, not a check.
Reply "QA passed: restructure steps 3 to 7", or "QA failed: restructure steps 3 to 7" and say what is wrong.

unverified: No Claude Code session has run 2.74.0 yet; every check drove the hooks with recorded payloads, and the settings gate was run end to end only in a scratch home folder
The menu wording in docs/cloud-session-setup.md comes from Claude Code's environment help, not from checking each app
The new Edit guard and the settings gate for tools other than Bash are proven only with simulated payloads, not a live Edit or Read

wrapup.summary: QA for restructure steps 3 to 7 (#381): settings and identity, safe git, design loop, writing rules and helper agents, house-rules 2.74.0.
wrapup.changing: Once you pass QA, a pull request takes 2.74.0 to the main branch. Set the two environment variables before your next session loads it.
